title: Ever, and never
goal: Build the "have done" form with *hafa* + sagnbót, and know exactly when to use it — and when the plain past is the right choice instead.
bekal: form the sagnbót of both weak and strong verbs
tell *ég fór* apart from *ég hef farið*
use *vera búinn að* like a native speaker

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Hefurðu séð norðurljósin?
dialogs.intro: Early October, and the nights are dark again. Sigga calls Búdí with a last-minute plan.

lines.speaker: Sigga:
lines.id: Budi, have you ever seen the northern lights?

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.text: Nei, ég hef aldrei séð þau. Ég hef bara séð myndir.
lines.id: No, I've never seen them. I've only seen pictures.
lines.literal: no, I have never seen them. I have only seen pictures.

lines.speaker: Sigga:
lines.text: Þá verðum við að laga það. Ég hef fylgst með spánni.
lines.id: Then we have to fix that. I've been following the forecast.
lines.literal: then must we to fix that. I have followed with forecast-the.

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.id: There's a forecast for the northern lights?

lines.speaker: Sigga:
lines.text: Já, alveg eins og veðurspá. Í kvöld er virknin sterk.
lines.id: Yes, just like a weather forecast. Tonight the activity is strong.
lines.literal: yes, all one and weather-forecast. in night is activity-the strong.

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.text: Hvert höfum við farið áður? Ég man ekki.
lines.id: Where have we been before? I don't remember.
lines.literal: where-to have we gone before? I remember not.

lines.speaker: Sigga:
lines.text: Við höfum aldrei farið saman. Þú hefur alltaf verið að læra!
lines.id: We've never gone anywhere together. You're always studying!
lines.literal: we have never gone together. you have always been to study!

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.text: Satt. Ég hef lært mikið en séð lítið.
lines.id: True. I've studied a lot but seen little.
lines.literal: true. I have studied much but seen little.

lines.speaker: Sigga:
lines.text: Í kvöld breytist það. Áttu hlýja úlpu?
lines.id: Tonight that changes. Do you have a warm jacket?
lines.literal: in night changes that. have-you warm jacket?

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.text: Ég keypti eina í síðustu viku.
lines.literal: I bought one in last week.

lines.speaker: Sigga:
lines.text: Fullkomið. Við förum klukkan tíu, út fyrir borgina.
lines.id: Perfect. We leave at ten, out of town.
lines.literal: perfect. we go at ten, out for town-the.

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.text: Loksins! Ég hef beðið eftir þessu í þrjá mánuði.
lines.id: Finally! I've been waiting for this for three months.
lines.literal: finally! I have waited after this in three months.

notes: **The pattern: *hafa* + sagnbót (supine).** *Ég **hef séð***, *ég **hef farið***, *ég **hef lært***. Only *hafa* changes form; the sagnbót stays the same for every subject — so once you know one sagnbót, it works for all six forms. Just like English *I have seen*, *she has seen*.

**The sagnbót always has the hvorugkyn form**, usually ending in **-að**, **-t**, or **-ið**: *talað*, *lært*, *farið*, *séð*, *verið*, *komið*. The neuter is used once again as the language's default form — a pattern you've seen since unit 3.

⚠️ **Ég keypti eina í síðustu viku, not ég hef keypt.** When the time is stated clearly (*í gær*, *í síðustu viku*, *árið 2020*), Icelandic uses the **plain past**. The "have done" form is used when the time is **not** stated, or when the effect is still felt now.

**Aldrei and alltaf almost always pair with this form**: *ég hef aldrei séð* (I've never seen), *þú hefur alltaf verið* (you've always been). Those two words are the surest sign that the "have done" form is needed.

**Bíða eftir + þágufall** — wait for something. *Ég hef beðið eftir þessu* — I've been waiting for this. Don't drop *eftir*; without it, *bíða* just means waiting with no object, like "wait" without "for".

**Northern lights forecasts really exist.** The Icelandic Met Office, *Veðurstofan*, publishes an aurora map every day showing two things: the strength of solar activity and cloud cover. Hunting the aurora without checking that map almost always ends in disappointment.

grammars.title: Hafa + sagnbót
body: Only the form of *hafa* changes. The sagnbót has one form for everyone — that's the easy part.
after: ***Ekki* comes after *hafa*, not after the sagnbót**: *Ég hef **ekki** séð það.* The *ekki* rule from unit 2 still applies exactly — it always follows the verb **that changes form**.
Questions are made as usual, by swapping the order: *Hefur þú séð?* → *Hefurðu séð?*

grammars.title: Forming the sagnbót
body: Three patterns, all with a distinctive ending. Strong verbs often take **-ið**; weak verbs take **-að** or **-t**.
after: ⚠️ *Drekka → drukkið* changes its vowel again, and not to the same vowel as the past (*drakk*). Strong verbs often have **three** different vowels: *drekka – drakk – drukkið*, *finna – fann – fundið*. English does it too — *drink – drank – drunk* — so learn them in threes.

**An everyday alternative that's just as common: *vera búinn að*.** *Ég er búinn að borða* = I've already eaten. *Búinn* follows the subject's gender: *búinn* (male), *búin* (female), *búið* (neuter). In conversation you'll actually hear this more often than *ég hef borðað*.

blocks.text: The difference works almost exactly like English *I went* versus *I have gone*, so you already have the instinct. The question is always the same: **is the time stated?**

blocks.title: Three deciding signals
items: **A specific time is stated** (*í gær*, *í fyrra*, *klukkan sjö*, *árið 2020*) → plain past. No exceptions.
**Aldrei, alltaf, einhvern tíma, aldrei áður** → the "have done" form.
**Something that started in the past and is still going on** (*í þrjá mánuði*, *síðan í ágúst*) → the "have done" form.

blocks.title: Four conditions that must all be met
items: **Darkness** — so only between September and April; in summer the sky never gets dark enough.
**Clear skies** — clouds beat even the strongest aurora. *Veðurstofan*'s cloud map matters more than the activity number.
**Away from city lights** — a twenty-minute drive out of Reykjavík is enough.
**Patience** — the aurora can appear for five minutes and then vanish for an hour. Bring a thermos, and wear a truly thick *úlpa*.

exercises.prompt: Write the sagnbót of these verbs.
Fill in the blanks with the right form of *hafa*.
Choose the right form: plain past or the "have done" form.
items: Ég ____ (fór, hef farið) til Þingvalla í gær.
Hún ____ (keypti, hefur keypt) úlpu í síðustu viku.
Við ____ (biðum, höfum beðið) í þrjá mánuði — og bíðum enn.
Þeir ____ (komu, hafa komið) klukkan sjö í morgun.
Have you ever seen the northern lights?
I've been waiting for three months.

answers: talað — lært — farið — séð — verið — komið
hef — Hefur — hefur — höfum — Hafið — hafa
fór — hef séð — keypti — höfum beðið — komu
Hefurðu séð norðurljósin? — Ég hef aldrei séð þau. — Við höfum aldrei farið saman. — Ég hef lært mikið. — Ég keypti eina í síðustu viku. — Ég hef beðið í þrjá mánuði.
